items.text: Bank feeds are up to date for every account, card and payment platform (Stripe, PayPal, Square).
items.why: Reconciliation is only as complete as the transactions you have.

items.text: All supplier bills dated in the month are entered, including ones still in the inbox.
items.why: A bill missing at month end understates expenses and accounts payable.

items.text: All sales invoices for work done in the month are raised.
items.why: Revenue belongs to the month the work was done (accruals basis).

items.text: Payroll for the month is posted, with super (AU) or pension and PAYE/NIC (UK) liabilities.
items.why: Wages and their on-costs are usually the largest expense.

items.text: Every bank and card account reconciles to the statement closing balance.
items.why: The bank statement is the one external, independent check on the ledger.

items.text: Clearing and suspense accounts are at zero, or every item in them is explained.
items.why: A balance left in suspense is an error waiting to be found by someone else.

items.text: Aged receivables and aged payables agree to the balance sheet control accounts.
items.why: A difference means a journal hit a control account directly.

items.text: The GST or VAT account agrees to the tax report for the period.
items.why: Manual journals to the tax account are the usual cause of a BAS or VAT return that does not tie up.

items.text: Payroll liabilities (PAYG, super, PAYE, pension) agree to the payroll reports.
items.why: Unpaid super or PAYE carries penalties; the balance must be what is actually owed.

items.text: Accrue expenses incurred but not yet billed (electricity, audit fees, contractor time).
items.why: Matching: the cost belongs to the month it was incurred.

items.text: Release one month of each prepayment (insurance, annual software) to expense.
items.why: A 12-month policy paid in January is 1/12 an expense each month.

items.text: Release deferred revenue earned this month; defer amounts billed in advance.
items.why: Revenue is recognised when the obligation is satisfied, not when billed.

items.text: Post depreciation and amortisation from the fixed asset register.
items.why: Spreads the cost of assets over the periods that benefit.

items.text: Adjust inventory to the count or the perpetual records, and post write-downs to NRV.
items.why: Closing stock drives cost of sales directly.

items.text: Review old receivables; update the allowance for credit losses or write off what will not be paid.
items.why: Prudence: expected losses are recognised, not hoped away.

items.text: Set last month's accruals to reverse on the first day of this month.
items.why: Otherwise the real bill arriving this month doubles the expense.

items.text: Read the trial balance: every balance on its normal side, nothing strange or unexplained.
items.why: A credit balance on an expense account or a debit on a liability is usually a mis-posting.

items.text: Compare the P&L with last month and with budget; explain big swings.
items.why: Analytical review catches what reconciliations miss, such as a missing rent bill.

items.text: Set the lock date in Xero or close the books in QBO.
items.why: Stops anyone changing a period that has been reported.

items.text: Send the management pack (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, aged reports).
items.why: The close is only useful if the owner sees the numbers while they still matter.
